exposure: Race (non-Hispanic White, non-Hispanic Black, other races)
Hospital type (rural vs urban, bed number - large vs medium)
outcome: Surgical errors (e.g., foreign body retained, anesthetic error, errors involving blood vessels, errors involving bladder)
Complications (e.g., mortality, postpartum hemorrhage, infection, hysterectomy)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 648,584 women who underwent cesarean delivery in the United States between 2012 and 2014.
finding: Among women undergoing cesarean delivery, 1.98% experienced a surgical error and 8.43% experienced a complication, with both individual- and hospital-level factors associated with these outcomes.
